criterion: Quarantine files with a measured single-file run over 30 s, plus measured-red files whose assertions or waiting failures require repair before returning to the blocking suite.
source: These ten entries are the dedicated files of the twelve-file study the stream inherited: one of the twelve, test/plugin-fill-scenarios.test.ts, was already back in the blocking shards before this change, one, test/api-role-first-page.test.ts, returns to them in the follow-up commit that carries the pull request's first run, and these ten stay listed. They were measured on GitHub Actions' ubuntu-24.04 runners after the speed-up stream madarch-64o5.176 landed (F1+F2, F3, F5-catalogue, F5-fill and F4). Each file ran alone in three independent runs of the F4 tree: 46044618928 (the pull request head 7b9499138, tree 83e9ef8f), 46045922097 (the merge 46be90c4a, the same tree) and 46046625374 (9b0b16da3, after the merge that followed). The seconds each of the nine stream entries records are the median of those three green complete-file measurements, and .github/workflows/single-file-timings.json carries the same number as that file's committed single-file evidence, which the slow-list check compares within 100 ms. test/catalogue-kind-relations.test.ts returned to the blocking shards on those three samples and then measured 33 641 ms and 34 019 ms in shard 1 of the pull request's two required runs (46063935769 and 46078818727) and 37 781 ms alone in the second run's confirmation, so it is listed again with that alone measurement, not the median of the three, and runs in its own named required job; the three standalone samples and the reviewed head's 25 315 ms stay as historical evidence. Entries of other tasks keep the note their own source names. test/fill-trace.test.ts carries its GitHub Actions runner measurement from run 46072517676 (ubuntu-24.04) on 2026-11-27: 33.686 s alone and 30.011 s inside shard 2.
note: A real fill pass of a small, already trimmed fixture costs 18.6-19.5 s on a runner (sample B's two status-work case fills; main's median for that fixture was 19.3 s before 0039), so a file that needs two passes cannot reach the 30 s bound whatever its data. The three samples of one tree also vary by up to 40% (owner-fill-path 66.10 s against 108.39 s), which is why a file at 32.72 s is not treated as an exit candidate. Each staying entry names the passes it pays and why they are its subject. The box numbers these entries carried before measured the 0039 candidate, where one fill cost 155.6 s against main's 19.3 s; those numbers are superseded by the runner samples above.

files.defect: The two cases drive a whole agent fill through the api role and the plugin's own turns, and both agent fills are the case's subject: 24.1 s and 9.6 s of its 33.7 s of case time in sample B. After the speed-up stream landed (F1+F2, F3, F5-catalogue, F5-fill and F4) the complete file is green on the runner in three samples of the F4 tree: 24.18 s, 36.96 s and 35.76 s (runs 46044618928, 46045922097 and 46046625374), median 35.76 s, which is the number this entry records. Its earlier runner measurement was 31.283 s alone and 38.304 s in shard 1 (run 45809866011).
files.replacement: No safe reduction is left: each case is an agent fill with its own turns, and one pass of an already trimmed fixture costs 18.6-19.5 s on the runner, so two passes cannot fit the bound without dropping a scenario. Both agent fill scenarios stay and the entry keeps its two cases. Stays a named required job in the slow-files matrix of .github/workflows/ci.yml until a green complete-file runner measurement at or below 30 s exits it; the shards exclude it, so the matrix job is its required coverage.

The allowed-to-fail nightly / quarantine job is not coverage.
